page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor supplying 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 48.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU in a typical compute-focused 1:2 resource ratio. The instance includes 35 MB of shared L3 cache, standard hardware cryptographic support including AES, and vector extensions up to AVX-512F. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth profile rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark metrics reflect the profile of a legacy multi-core architecture. Single-core throughput ranks in lower brackets, evident from a Geekbench single-core score of 945.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.08, and single-threaded gzip compression performance of 19.08 GB/sec. When parallelized across all 24 virtual cores, compute capacity rises to the mid-tier category, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 18444.17, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7148.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 83.08 GB/sec. Memory operations show stable mid-range bandwidth, recording 90.83 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 52.97 GB/sec on uncached writes.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-conscious compute density for organizations needing core scale over expansive RAM pools. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires cloud disks for all I/O paths, and network throughput of 4 Gbps bounds data-intensive transfer pipelines. The instance is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, compiling software suites, static web traffic handling, and distributed horizontally scaling worker nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 12 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, it maintains a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads. The configuration includes no integrated GPU and no local storage, requiring network-attached storage across a 4 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals modest single-thread capabilities offset by steady multi-core performance, achieving 18444.17 in PassMark CPU tests and 7148.0 in Geekbench multi-core. With 16.86 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.88 GB/sec static web serving throughput, this instance is appropriate for multi-threaded compiling, distributed microservices, web fleets, and parallel background batch jobs.
